answers.question: Question 10: Your inputs name no tools, so here is the smallest tool set in which every write has one call and every fact the agent needs before it acts has a read. (1) Look up the customer's orders: returns each order with its status, line items, total paid and payment method, and its refund or none; it changes nothing, and it can get no answer. (2) Cancel an order, by order number: answers cancelled, is rejected because the order has shipped, or gets no answer, which may or may not have cancelled the order. (3) Issue the refund for an order, by order number: returns the refund, pending or issued; returns a refund with status failed on a terminal error; creates no refund on a transient error; or times out. (4) Create a follow-up task for staff, by order number and reason (refund not issued, refund status unknown, cancellation unknown): answers created, or times out. Do you confirm this tool set? Claims put to the owner: C-24, C-43.
answers.recommended: Yes: these four calls, with these outcomes.
answers.reply:
> Confirmed, with four changes:
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Question 11: The agent passes on a refund amount from the order system. What should the agent do when the refund the order system returns, or a later lookup shows, is for an amount other than the total paid that the customer said yes to? The shortest path where it matters: the customer says yes to "cancel HG-10482 and refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242"; the order is cancelled; the refund call returns a refund of $43.20. Claims put to the owner: C-16.
answers.recommended: The agent makes no further change, tells the customer the amount the order system returned, and creates a follow-up task for staff with the reason refund status unknown.

answers.question: Question 12: Your answers say two things about a follow-up call that times out. One says: "handoff timeout not retried". Another says: "On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support." Under the first, after one timed-out follow-up call the agent tells the customer to contact Harbor Goods support. Under the second, it sends the call once more first, which creates no second task because the call is idempotent on order and reason, and only after a second time-out tells the customer to contact Harbor Goods support. Which holds? Claims put to the owner: C-37.
answers.recommended: Retry once: the agent sends a timed-out follow-up call once more, and when it times out again tells the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
answers.reply: > 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.

answers.question: Question 13: Your order system has no docs, so I compared it with common payment systems. In those, repeating a refund request is safe only when the system recognizes the repeat (Stripe's docs: "if a connection error occurs, you can safely repeat the request without risk of creating a second object or performing the update twice", when the request carries the same idempotency key). Your answers have the agent send the refund call once more after a time-out, and allow at most one refund per order. If a second refund call for an order that already has a refund creates no second refund and returns the existing one, that retry is safe. If it could create a second refund, the agent must not send the refund call again after a time-out, and looks up the refund instead. Which holds for your order system? Claims put to the owner: C-29.
answers.recommended: A second refund call for an order that already has a refund creates no second refund and returns the existing one.
answers.reply:
> - Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund.
> The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B).
> The agent may retry it.
